newsletter.subject: Halloween on Sevier Avenue: an eleven-stop costume crawl, a haunted pink house and a paddle under the stars

feature.label: Old Sevier
feature.title: The Old Sevier Halloween Pub Crawl puts eleven neighborhood stops on one passport Saturday
feature.deck: Halloween lands on a Saturday, and the merchants' association is turning the whole avenue into the party: a free passport, a costume, and a coffee roaster, a pizza place and a cocktail lounge on the same route.

facts.label: When
facts.value: Sat Oct 31 · all day, on each stop's own hours

facts.label: Where
facts.value: The Old Sevier District: Sevier Avenue, Island Home Avenue and Barber Street

facts.label: Cost
facts.value: Free to play · a purchase gets the passport stamped

facts.label: How it works
facts.value: Pick up a passport at any participating stop · visit six or more and you are entered to win a prize package from the district's businesses

facts.label: The eleven stops
facts.value: Alliance Brewing · Fly by Night · Hi-Wire Brewing · Honeybee Coffee · Printshop Beer Co. · Redbud Kitchen · Sevier Ave Burger Co. · South Coast Pizza · SouthSide Garage · The Pink Cactus · Trailhead Beer Market

facts.label: Dress code
facts.value: Costumes highly encouraged

facts.label: Parking
facts.value: Riverwalk Garage at the west end, the gravel lot under the James White Parkway bridge at the east end, the public lot at the east end of Suttree Landing Park

facts.label: Weather
facts.value: Mostly cloudy and 76 · showers possible after dark · clocks fall back at 2 AM

body.text: The Old Sevier District, the merchants' association for the Sevier Avenue corridor, posted the route Saturday: on October 31 its Halloween Pub Crawl is back, with eleven neighborhood businesses on a single passport and the whole day to work through them. Grab a passport at whichever stop you reach first, get it stamped with a purchase at each place you visit, and hit six or more to be entered for a prize package put together by the district's businesses. There is no cover and no ticket; the association's own word for it is a neighborhood in on the spooky-season shenanigans.
A route you can walk

The list is the avenue end to end, and it is not all beer. Honeybee Coffee is a stop, so is South Coast Pizza, Redbud Kitchen and Sevier Ave Burger Co., which puts breakfast, lunch and dinner on the passport alongside Alliance, Hi-Wire, Printshop and Trailhead's taps, Fly by Night's cocktail list and the Pink Cactus's karaoke rooms. SouthSide Garage opens at noon and runs to midnight on Saturday. Everything sits within about a mile, from Printshop and Trailhead on Island Home Avenue to Hi-Wire on Barber Street, so the sensible plan is to park once and walk it in costume.
The stops have their own nights

Several of the eleven have Halloween programming that starts as the crawl winds down. The Pink Cactus turns into a haunted house party with free karaoke after nine, Hi-Wire's drag show and costume contest starts at nine, Trailhead has Four Legged Dog on the patio at seven, and just off the list The 808 has Bear Grillz, so the passport can end at a show. The forecast is mostly cloudy and 76 with a chance of showers after dark, and the clocks go back an hour at 2 AM, which the late stops are counting as a bonus hour of Halloween.

body.text: Belltower, the goth night Temple runs, has the Pink Cactus on Halloween itself. Its post with the venue describes a decorated haunted house party: a dark dance party downstairs with live DJs spinning goth music all night, Verena Noctem, Sara Alured and Cemetery Sex among them, local vendors, the outdoor bar back open, and the venue's treat, free karaoke in all four rooms after nine, with a request to let everyone have a turn. Entry is fifteen dollars at the gate, 18 and up, costumes encouraged.

The hosts have extended hours for the night and are counting the end of daylight saving time, which falls at 2 AM Sunday, as a bonus hour: the party runs until the clock says two. It is the last stop on Saturday's pub crawl route for anyone still in costume, and the hosts warn that parking will be tight, so carpool or rideshare in.

stories.deck: Two guided hours on the water under the stars with a naturalist, a headlamp and a boat provided; the full-moon paddles are done for the year, so this is the dark-sky one.

body.text: Ijams Nature Center's Starlight Paddle is a two-hour guided trip on the Tennessee River after sunset on Friday, October 30, from seven to nine. Naturalists lead it from the boat dock at Ijams River Landing, pointing out the plants, animals and rock along the bank and the night sky above it, and the park provides the kayak, the life vest and the headlamp. It is for ages 14 and up, with anyone under 18 accompanied by an adult, and costs $45.
The practical part

Park at Ijams River Landing itself, down the road between the main visitor center and Meads Quarry, not at either of those lots. The park notes that its launch and dock have accessible elements but do not meet ADA requirements for a fully accessible dock, and asks anyone who needs accommodations to write before buying a ticket. Last weekend's Hunter Moon paddle was the last full-moon date of the season, so Friday's is the darker sky, and the forecast is clear: mostly sunny all day, into the 50s by the time the boats come in.

stories.deck: An hour with Ijams Nature Center's new opossum and the naturalist who looks after it: how the only marsupial in Tennessee lives, and why it is nothing to be scared of.

body.text: Ijams Nature Center has a new animal ambassador, an opossum, and Playing 'Possum on Saturday, October 31, from eleven to noon is the public's first scheduled hour with it. The park's listing promises a look at the lifestyle and adaptations of opossums, which is a long list: North America's only marsupial, a pouch, a prehensile tail, a tick appetite that makes it a gardener's friend, and the famous faint that gives the program its name. Ten dollars, with free parking for the hour if you check in a few minutes early. It runs again Friday, November 6, at six for anyone whose Halloween morning is spoken for, and it pairs with the free bat storytime at the Nature Playscape down Island Home Avenue from ten to noon.

body.text: Ijams Nature Center's Renew in Nature is a two-hour meditative workshop on Sunday, November 1, from ten to noon: a morning of nature meditation with yoga, a sound bath and a forest bathing session, in the park's words, split between the Miller Building and the Homesite Pavilion on the historic Ijams family homesite. Forest bathing is the Japanese practice of walking slowly and paying attention in the woods, and the pavilion sits at the edge of them. It is $40, registration on the park's calendar, and it falls on the first morning after the clocks go back, so ten o'clock will feel like eleven. Rain showers are likely Sunday; the yoga and the sound bath are under roof.

body.text: Earl's, the bar and kitchen on Waterfront Drive at Suttree Landing, runs a different special every day from eleven to ten, and this is a week without a game on top of it: the Vols have Saturday off before Kentucky comes to town on November 7, so the game-day board stays in the drawer. Thursday is ten-dollar Patrón mango ritas, Friday nine-dollar spicy pineapple ritas, Saturday eight-dollar house margaritas for anyone in costume or out of it, and Sunday seven-dollar mimosas and Bloody Marys, with the Titans at the Bengals at one on the screens. Thursday and Friday are sunny and in the mid-70s for the river tables; Sunday brings the showers.
